from.place: proof, finite duality identifies the right adjoint for a finite morphism and describes the counit

title: Finite Grothendieck duality as derived Hom with counit evaluation
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $K$ be an object of $D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category] (bounded below with quasi-coherent cohomology). Let $f^!K$ denote the right adjoint image for $Rf_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$, compatible with the $f_*\mathcal O_X$-module structure, $Rf_*f^!K\simeq R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(f_*\mathcal O_X,K)$. Under this canonical isomorphism, the adjunction counit $Rf_*f^!K\to K$ is induced by evaluation at the unit section $1\in f_*\mathcal O_X$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-affine-derived-hom-evaluation-counit] to get an ambient scalar right adjoint H, its adjunction adjH, iota and the Hom identification dH at K with its evaluation counit. Use the component e of adjA.rightAdjointUniq adjH (from rhoR to H) and define d = rho.mapIso(e) followed by dH. Associativity and the Mathlib rightAdjointUniq_hom_app_counit identity give the required evaluation equation for the specified adjA.

Use [lem-sc-finite-twisted-inverse-bounded-below] with the given adjunction to prove that a(K) is bounded below. Then [lem-sc-finite-affine-adjoint-counit-comparison] gives c, phi and the second counit equation.

Combine the independently constructed iota,d and c,phi and their two equations into the existential conclusion. No existence theorem for a geometric right adjoint is needed because adj is already an input.
